hypothesis: Theorem SA-1 (paper papers/sufficient_antecedents/paper.md) predicts that four canonical inductive-bias regimes (linear ICA, sparse-linear ICA, auxiliary-variable iVAE, interventional CRL) each satisfy Condition (I) local separation and Condition (II) cross-u coherence on the 4-bit Boolean world; the finest common refinement of each antecedent's local screens equals the latent Z-partition exactly (up to trivial refinement for the interventional case whose observational screen already gives Z).

gates.ATP_SA1_LOCAL_SEPARATION_AT_EVERY_ANTECE: For every antecedent (LinearICA, SparseLinearICA, AuxIVAE, InterventionalCRL), each of its local screens is a non-trivial partition of X (strictly more than 1 block and strictly fewer than |X| = 16 blocks).
gates.ATP_SA1_CROSS_U_INTERSECTION_REFINES_TRU: The finest common refinement of every antecedent's local screens is at least as fine as the true Z-partition.
gates.ATP_SA1_NONTRIVIAL_INTERSECTIONS_EQUAL_T: For LinearICA, SparseLinearICA, and AuxIVAE, the intersection equals the true Z-partition exactly.
gates.ATP_SA1_INTERVENTIONAL_INTERSECTION_REFI: For InterventionalCRL, the intersection refines the true Z-partition.

compute.sampling: exact enumeration of the 16-element Boolean world; no Monte Carlo
